channel.title: Business Insider Nederland - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Nederland (businessinsider.nl)

item.title: The US is facing a wrongful-death lawsuit after a lethal strike on a boat it says was smuggling drugs
item.description: Two Trinidadian nationals were said to be among six people killed by a US strike. The lawsuit characterized the strike as 'unlawful.'

item.title: Former Citi executive pleads guilty in case involving the drugging and sexual assault of women
item.description: Former Citi managing director Edward Gene Smith pleaded guilty to luring women to New York so that he could drug and sexually assault them.

item.title: Elon Musk hurls insults at Vinod Khosla after VC founder tries to poach Musk's employees
item.description: Elon Musk hurled insults at Vinod Khosla after the VC founder accused Musk of promoting racism and urged some of Musk's employees to quit.

item.title: Alexander bros' trial: The most striking revelations from day 1 of the criminal case
item.description: Former high-end real estate brokers, Tal and Oren, are accused of sexually assaulting dozens of women with their brother, Alon Alexander.

item.title: Where to buy tickets for the sold-out BTS 2026-2027 world tour: Full schedule and prices
item.description: The hype around BTS' return is real, and seats are mostly sold out for the group's 2026-2027 tour. Here's where to score highly coveted tickets.

item.title: Read Sam Altman's internal Slack message to employees saying ICE 'is going too far'
item.description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman privately wrote that part of being patriotic "is the American duty to push back against overreach."

item.title: Paramount+ got about 1 million new subscribers the day of its first UFC event, an exec told staffers
item.description: Paramount+ snagged about a million new customers on the day of its first UFC event, an exec told employees, as close to 5 million viewers tuned in.

item.title: Some Amazon employees get 'Project Dawn' calendar invitation discussing upcoming job cuts
item.description: The invitation was written by Amazon executive Colleen Aubrey. It was cancelled soon after being sent, stoking confusion among some employees.

item.title: Tiffany & Co. is setting its sights on the gold girlies
item.description: LVMH is pushing Tiffany toward gold and high jewelry, where it sees higher demand, and away from silver jewelry.

item.title: The CEO of $2 billion Harvey rival Legora says he still interviews everyone and asks this question
item.description: The Legora CEO, who cofounded the startup in 2023, said that he's looking for people who have "raw grit" and don't mind late hours.
